newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Englishwoman identifies soldiers in Cyprus attack.
newsitem.headline: Englishwoman identifies soldiers in Cyprus attack.

text.p: An English tourist on Thursday identified in court three British soldiers as having been involved in a vicious attack against her and two friends at a Cyprus seaside resort this month.
"It happened very fast but I cannot forget their faces," said Claire Harbour, 22.

Five soldiers -- Roger Bell, 26, Tim Carter, 20, Steven Wolstencroft, 26, Steven Girvan, 20, and Stuart Spencer, 20 -- face charges of causing actual bodily harm to Harbour and grievous bodily harm to holidaymakers Shane Bell and Barry Ford, both 23.
The soldiers, stationed at the British military base of Dhekelia in southwestern Cyprus, have pleaded not guilty. Shane Bell and Roger Bell are not related.
Harbour told a court in the coastal town of Larnaca that she identified Bell, Carter and Wolstencroft as being involved in the attack.
Harbour, a nursery nurse from southeast London, said Roger Bell attacked Ford as they left a nightclub in the Ayia Napa resort on August 2 after the two exchanged words.

"He followed us from behind then walked in front of us and turned around, hitting Barry on the face with a punch. The next thing I remember was Barry being kicked and punched on the ground by approximately eight men," she said, fighting back tears.
Ford suffered a shattered wrist in the attack, while Shane Bell needed surgery on a fractured jawbone.
"I tried to stop them...I remember my hair being pulled back and being told "Not to worry, it'll all be over in a minute," she said, identifying Roger Bell as the person who restrained her.
The court ordered the trial to reconvene on Monday.
All three tourists are suing the five Britons for damages for a joint sum of up to 25,000 Cyprus pounds ($45,000).
The accused are riflemen with the 600-strong Kings Regiment based at the British base of Dhekelia.
The attack prompted the British base authorities to impose a ban on visits to Ayia Napa by members of the Kings regiment, just one month after another ban on soldiers' visits to the area was lifted.

The restrictions were first imposed in September 1994 after the brutal killing of a Danish tour guide by three members of the Royal Greenjackets regiment. They are now serving a life sentence in Cyprus's central prison.
Around 3,500 British troops are stationed at two military bases Britain has retained in Cyprus since independence in 1960. ($=0.55 pounds)
